text.p: Spanish government bonds start flat on Friday morning amid dull trade awaiting for German job data in the morning and U.S. job figure later, dealers said.
Despite modest gains were seen likely, they expected a narrow trading range before the Sunday's EU economic ministers meeting in Luxembourg.
"It's very quiet, here. What people are expecting is a clearer outlook on EMU," a dealer in Madrid said.
With little domestic news in sight, the long bond future was likely to stay between support at 115.75 and resistance at 116.21, chartists added.
The 10-year spread over Bunds was trading this morning at 76 basis points, unchanged from yesterday's evening.

Dealers said they were expecting the market over the next week to focus on the announcement of benign May inflation data. May CPI, scheduled for June 13, is expected to show a further reduction from the April 1.7 percent year-on-year.
"But so far we haven't see any relevant movement in the short end," a dealer in Madrid said.
